% Numbers come from results/*.csv; do not edit by hand.

\paragraph{Complementary coverage}
The preceding comparison gives every client the same construction questions, so sharing mainly mixes
sources. We therefore construct a second, harder setting in which coverage itself is complementary. The
60 construction questions are partitioned into four disjoint sets of 15 (seed 20261108), and client $c$
keeps only its own 25 experiences on the questions in its set. A single client therefore holds 375
experiences covering a quarter of the construction space, while the union of the four local pool covers
all 60 questions with 1{,}500 experiences. Three regimes are compared: \emph{Local-only} (the requesting
client's 375 experiences), \emph{Shared-matched} (a 375-entry pool drawn from the union, covering all 60
questions with six or seven entries each and at most 94 entries per client), rebuilt from three
preselected seeds, and \emph{Shared-full-hetero} (the 1{,}500-entry union). This exposure is constructed
retrospectively from a corpus in which every client originally saw the same questions; it is not a
record of clients that sampled disjoint tasks online.

\paragraph{Results}
Local-only reaches 81.45\% (95\% CI [72.36, 89.82]), Shared-matched 80.48\% ([71.76, 88.43]) and
Shared-full-hetero 80.73\% ([71.82, 88.73]). Sharing experience that covers the three quarters of the
construction space a client has never seen does not raise accuracy: the paired difference is
$-0.97$ percentage points ([-4.06, +2.12]). Expanding the matched pool to the full union likewise
changes nothing measurable ($+0.24$ points, [-2.73, +3.09]), and the overall union-versus-local gap is
$-0.73$ points ([-3.82, +2.36]). The three matched pools individually score 80.55\%, 78.73\% and
82.18\%, a spread that again exceeds every between-policy difference. Retrieval confirms that the
manipulation is real: in the matched pools 3.6 of the five retrieved experiences come from clients other
than the requester, and their Top-5 sets overlap only 21\% with the full union. Within this controlled
setting, cross-client coverage therefore does not translate into measurable accuracy gains; the
contribution of sharing remains the reduction in communication and storage cost rather than an accuracy
uplift.
